WV12-P02.5.note: The narrator laughs at the swarm and still grins at the memory, and every bee episode is told as comic, so amusement fits; the present-tense grin rules out wistfulness and nothing expresses worry, criticism, or admiration of the hives.

exclusions.B: Each new mark sits a little below the last.
exclusions.C: In January the council will vote on whether to pay for a repair in lime mortar, which the masons say the old brick needs in place of cheap cement, or to have the chimney pulled down.
exclusions.E: The storm two winters ago opened a crack from the chimney's top toward the roofline, and every month since, Reyburn has gone up the roof ladder to pencil a mark at its lower end.

support: On every windy night since the storm I have lain awake listening for the sound of falling brick from the hill, and each morning I look out to see whether the chimney is still standing.
If the vote goes the other way, or a winter gale finds the crack first, the swifts will come back in May to an empty patch of sky above a heap of brick.
WV12-P04.5.note: The writer lies awake listening for falling brick and doubts the vote, which is apprehension about a loss still ahead rather than sadness over one already suffered.
